text: Ant Colony Optimization (ACO), formalized by Marco Dorigo, solves optimization problems by having artificial 'ants':
choices: Report all candidate solutions to a central controller that picks the best
Each independently compute the complete optimal solution on their own
Deposit virtual pheromone on solution components and follow trails probabilistically, with evaporation preventing premature convergence
Share one global variable holding the single best solution found so far
explanation: ACO is a formalization of stigmergic foraging: ants lay virtual pheromone on good solution components and are probabilistically drawn to strong trails, while evaporation keeps the search from locking in too early. There is no central controller, and no individual ant represents or computes the whole solution — the answer emerges from distributed interaction.
